To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AZD8835 promotes anti-tumor activity by enhancing CD8+ T cells and suppressing T-regs.

(1) PI3Kα inhibition alone or in combination with PD-1 blockade is not sufficient to promote CD8+ T cells anti-tumor activity in a syngeneic mouse model; (2) PI3Kδ inhibition alone or in combinations with PD-1 inhibition does not promote CD8+T cell anti-tumor activity; (3) Dual PI3Kα and δ inhibition promotes anti-tumour activity through enhancing CD8+ T cell effector functions and survival
AZD8835 is a potent anti-tumor agent that acts by promoting CD8+ T cell activity and memory in syngeneic mouse models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of new immunomodulatory compounds and the development of new immunotherapeutic strategies for cancer treatment.
the role of PI3K isoform inhibition in the tumor microenvironment.
the development and characterization of PI3K inhibitors, specifically AZD8835 (dual PI3Kαδ inhibitor) and AZD8186 (selective PI3Kδ inhibitor), for the treatment of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the PI3Kα and PI3Kα/dual inhibitor, AZD8833, has potent anti-tumor activity and promotes tumor immune microenvironment changes in mouse syngenic models, which is associated with enhanced CD8+ T-cells activation and memory.
PI3Kα and PI3Kα/delta inhibitors have been shown to have anti-tumor effects through immune mechanisms, and that this effect is not limited to PI3Kδ inhibition.
AZD8835 is a potent anti-tumor agent that can enhance anti-tumor immunity and that this is independent of its effects on tumor cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PI3Kα and δ inhibition promotes anti-tumour immunity through direct enhancement effector CD8 T-cell function and viability.
PI3Kα and PI3Kα/delta inhibitors are potent immunomodulators and can be used as monotherapies to treat cancers.
PI3Kα and δ inhibition promotes anti-tumoral immunity by directly improving the function of effector CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells, independent of its effects on T-regs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PI3Kα and δ isoform inhibitors can be effective as immunotherapeutics in the treatment of cancer, independent of the direct effects on the tumor.

PI3Kα and δ inhibitors can have a profound effect on the immune system, and that this is not necessarily mediated by effects on T-regs or myeloid cells, which are the most commonly investigated immune cells in the tumor microenvironment.
AZD8835 is a novel immunonocology agent, independent of effects of tumor cells.
